questions.scenario: A support application stores help articles that were embedded by using the text-embedding-3-small model with the default number of dimensions. You are writing the code that searches the articles by using a user's question.
questions.question: How should you generate the vector for the user's question?

options.text: Use text-embedding-3-large so that the query vector contains more detail
options.why: Vectors from different models are not comparable, and the 3,072-dimension output would not match the stored 1,536-dimension vectors.

options.text: Use text-embedding-3-small with the same dimensions setting that was used for the articles
options.why: Correct. Query and document vectors must come from the same model with the same number of dimensions to be compared meaningfully.

options.text: Use the chat model deployment and ask it to return a list of numbers
options.why: A chat model does not produce embeddings in the same vector space as the stored articles.

options.text: Send the raw question text to the database and let the vector index convert it
options.why: The vector index compares vectors. The application must generate the query embedding before it runs the search.

questions.explanation: Vector search compares distances inside one vector space. The question must be embedded with the same model and the same dimensions as the stored content.

questions.question: A container holds 12 million product embeddings. Searches must return results in a few milliseconds at a low cost per query. Returning one fewer of the true top 10 matches occasionally is acceptable. Which type of search should you implement?

options.text: Exact k-nearest neighbor search over every vector
options.why: Exact search compares the query with all 12 million vectors, so latency and cost grow with the data.

options.text: Approximate nearest neighbor search by using an index such as DiskANN or HNSW
options.why: Correct. An ANN index checks a small part of the data and trades a small amount of recall for much lower latency and cost.

options.text: A keyword search on the product name
options.why: Keyword search does not find items by meaning and is not a vector search.

options.text: A range index on the embedding property
options.why: A range index supports equality and range filters on scalar values, not similarity ranking of vectors.

questions.explanation: When a small loss of recall is acceptable and the data set is large, an approximate nearest neighbor index gives the best latency and cost.

questions.question: You are preparing 2,000 long PDF manuals for a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) application that stores vectors in Azure Database for PostgreSQL. Which TWO actions will improve the relevance of retrieved content?

options.text: Split each manual into passages of a few hundred tokens before embedding
options.why: Correct. Smaller chunks give each vector one focused idea, so the search returns the relevant passage.

options.text: Store metadata such as document ID and tenant ID with each chunk and filter on it during retrieval
options.why: Correct. Metadata filters keep results to the right document set and prevent results from other tenants.

options.text: Embed each complete manual as a single vector
options.why: A single vector for a long document averages many topics together, which reduces precision.

options.text: Use a different embedding model for every manual
options.why: Vectors from different models cannot be compared, so the search results would be meaningless.

questions.explanation: Chunking and metadata filters are the two main levers for retrieval quality in a RAG pattern.

questions.question: You store OpenAI text embeddings and must configure the distance function for similarity search. The embeddings are normalized to a length of 1. Which distance function is the recommended default for text similarity?

options.text: Euclidean distance, where a higher value means more similar
options.why: For Euclidean distance a lower value means more similar, and cosine is the usual default for text embeddings.

options.text: Cosine similarity
options.why: Correct. Cosine compares the direction of vectors and is the usual default for text embeddings.

options.text: Hamming distance
options.why: Hamming distance compares binary strings and is not used for floating-point text embeddings in these services.

options.text: Manhattan distance
options.why: Manhattan distance is not one of the distance functions offered for these vector policies.

questions.explanation: Cosine similarity is the standard choice for text embeddings. Because OpenAI embeddings are normalized, dot product gives the same ranking.

questions.question: An application must answer repeated customer questions quickly by reusing previous answers when a new question has a similar meaning, even if the wording differs. Response time must be under a few milliseconds. Which solution should you use?

options.text: A semantic cache that stores question embeddings in a vector index in Azure Managed Redis
options.why: Correct. Redis keeps vectors in memory and can find a previous question with a similar meaning very quickly.

options.text: A key-value cache in Azure Managed Redis that uses the exact question text as the key
options.why: An exact-text key only matches identical wording, so similar questions would miss the cache.

options.text: A nightly batch job that exports all answers to Azure Blob Storage
options.why: A batch export does not provide millisecond similarity lookups.

options.text: A larger chat model deployment
options.why: A larger model increases cost and latency and does not reuse previous answers.

questions.explanation: A semantic cache embeds each question and searches a Redis vector index, so similar questions can reuse a stored answer.
